title: Demo environment observability & alerts (dashboard freshness, error spikes, capacity) + Slack routing
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Problem
The demo tenant needs to be reliable in front of prospects, but the most common failures (empty dashboards, sudden error spikes, capacity/quota issues) are currently detected by an SE in the moment. We need demo-specific monitoring + alerting that is actionable for GTM and points to the right runbooks.

Scope
1) Metrics and dashboards for the demo environment only (tagged by org_id / tenant label).
2) Alerts:
   - Dashboard freshness (telemetry ingestion + synthetic traffic signal)
   - Error rate spikes (API + streaming)
   - Capacity/quota pressure (429s, queueing, throttling signals)
3) Slack alert route that is GTM-friendly (low noise) and points to the healthcheck + reset runbook.

Non-goals
- PagerDuty escalation for every alert (we’ll start with Slack + owner triage, then revisit once we have noise data).
- Building a full “demo mode” UI in Console.

Definitions / key signals
- Demo tenant identifier: env=demo AND demo_org_slug=redwood-demo (from control plane) OR explicit allowlist of demo org IDs.
- “Dashboard freshness” = telemetry pipeline is ingesting demo events AND Console queries for demo project return non-empty within a defined lookback.
- Primary health surface for SEs remains the demo tenant healthcheck endpoint (ENG-4862); alerts should link to it.

Implementation plan
A) Tagging & routing
- Ensure all demo-tenant requests/events are labeled with env=demo and demo_org_id (control plane -> gateway -> telemetry).
- Add a dedicated Slack destination: #demo-alerts (readable by Sales Engineering + SRE + Eng Platform).
- Add an alert grouping key: alertname + demo_org_id + region to prevent alert floods.

B) Dashboards (Console / internal monitoring)
- Create a “Demo Environment Overview” dashboard with:
  - Requests/min (by region)
  - Error rate (4xx/5xx) and streaming disconnect rate
  - P50/P95 latency
  - 429 rate + quota rejection counts
  - Telemetry ingest lag + last_seen_demo_event timestamp
  - Synthetic traffic job last_success timestamp (from ENG-4833)

C) Alert rules (initial thresholds; tune based on 2 weeks of field data)
1) DEMO_DASHBOARD_FRESHNESS_STALE
- Trigger when: last_seen_demo_event > 15m OR telemetry_ingest_lag_p95 > 10m
- Severity: warn
- Action: run synthetic traffic job; verify ingestion; check project/time range; link runbook

2) DEMO_CONSOLE_EMPTY_STATE_REGRESSION (guardrail)
- Trigger when: healthcheck reports console_query_empty=true for demo project for > 10m
- Severity: warn
- Action: follow empty dashboards playbook (time range, project selector, ingestion)

3) DEMO_API_ERROR_SPIKE
- Trigger when: 5xx rate > 2% for 5m OR error budget burn > 10x baseline (demo env)
- Severity: high
- Action: switch demo to backup mode; link status + known issues; optional failover region

4) DEMO_STREAMING_DISCONNECT_SPIKE
- Trigger when: streaming_disconnect_rate > 1% for 5m in a region
- Severity: warn/high (warn if single region; high if multi-region)
- Action: use alternate region; fall back to non-streaming steps; link known workaround (see SUP-4302)

5) DEMO_CAPACITY_PRESSURE
- Trigger when: 429 rate > 1% for 3m OR queue_time_p95 > 2s for 5m OR GPU utilization sustained > 90% for 10m on demo pool
- Severity: warn
- Action: reduce parallel load; move a demo to a secondary namespace/project; link capacity & quotas runbook

Alert message format (Slack)
- Title: [DEMO] <alertname> (<region>)
- Body:
  - What broke (one sentence)
  - Impact (what an AE/SE will see)
  - Immediate workaround (1–2 bullets)
  - Links: healthcheck URL, reset runbook, capacity runbook, dashboard link

Acceptance criteria
- Alerts only fire for demo tenant/org IDs and do not leak/trigger on customer traffic.
- #demo-alerts receives:
  - one test alert per rule during validation
  - meaningful context + runbook link
- SE can resolve the top two issues without Eng involvement:
  - empty dashboards (freshness)
  - throttling/429s due to demo load
- Noise check: after 2 weeks, alert volume <= 3/day average (excluding planned load tests).

Validation plan
- Run synthetic traffic generator preset for 20 minutes; confirm dashboards populate.
- Simulate empty dashboards by stopping synthetic traffic; verify freshness alert triggers within 15m.
- Trigger error spike by forcing a known-safe 500 test route in demo-only project; verify alert + grouping.
- Trigger 429 by lowering quota in demo namespace; verify capacity pressure alert and runbook usefulness.

Links / references
- Eng SRE demo SLOs: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/demo-environment-slos.json
- Demo tenant reset runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/demo-tenant-reset-runbook.json
- Capacity and quotas runbook: sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/demo-capacity-and-quotas-runbook.json
- Related issues/PRs: ENG-4833 synthetic traffic; ENG-4862 healthcheck; ENG-4894 parallel demos support; PR-28610 alert routing & dashboards

Rollout
- Phase 1: ship dashboards + freshness + capacity alerts to #demo-alerts (warn severity)
- Phase 2: add error spike + streaming disconnect alerts, tune thresholds after 1 week
- Phase 3: document in internal demo guide + include in SE certification checklist
comments: 2026-01-12 (Allison Grant): Kicked off with Logan (telemetry) + Chloe (Console). We have env=demo available at gateway, but demo_org_id isn’t consistently propagated into all telemetry events. I’ll take an action item to add a fallback allowlist based on org_id until tagging is complete.

2026-01-16 (Logan Wright): Added demo_org_id tag to request metrics in the API gateway pipeline; older events (eval runs) still missing tag. Suggest healthcheck reads from control plane directly for ‘last request seen’ as a more reliable freshness source.

2026-01-21 (Sean Gallagher): +1 to using healthcheck as the canonical freshness computation. We should alert on healthcheck failing freshness rather than trying to replicate logic in 3 places. Please ensure Slack message includes workaround steps for SEs (run synthetic traffic job; verify time range; confirm correct project).

2026-01-24 (Allison Grant): Drafted alert rules and shared with Markus Klein for field sanity check. Main concern: avoid spamming #sales. Proposal: route to #demo-alerts only, and only post ‘high’ severity to #eng-sre as FYI.

2026-01-28 (Markus Klein): Strong request from SE team: include ‘What will I see in the demo?’ line at top of alert. Also link directly to the healthcheck report output rather than a generic dashboard.

2026-02-03 (Allison Grant): Implemented demo dashboard + alert grouping. Ran validation: freshness alert fired at 16m after stopping synthetic traffic (expected). Capacity pressure fired when quota lowered. Adjusted thresholds to reduce flapping (added 3m sustain window).

2026-02-07 (Sean Gallagher): Reviewed Slack templates. Approved. Please add a brief note to the reset runbook: if freshness alert is firing, do NOT reset first—run synthetic job and check ingestion lag to avoid unnecessary resets.

2026-02-14 (Allison Grant): Shipped to prod demo env. Test alerts posted to #demo-alerts. Updated internal demo guide with dashboard link + how to interpret alerts. Marking Done; follow-up tuning task to be filed after 2 weeks of noise data.
